tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Reads the full content of a file from the given path.

path.description: Absolute or relative path of the file to read

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Writes content to a file at the given path. Overwrites existing content.

path.description: Absolute or relative path of the file to write

content.description: Text content to write into the file

tools.name: search_file
tools.description: Searches specified Windows drives, or all available drive letters if none are specified, for a file by name and optional extension. Returns the full path of the first matching file, or 'No file found' if no match exists.

name.description: The file name or filename prefix to search for, without the extension if using the extension parameter.

drive.description: Optional list of drive letters to search, such as ['C', 'D'] or ['C:', 'D:']. If omitted or null, searches all drive letters from C to Z.

extension.description: Optional file extension without a leading dot, such as 'pdf', 'txt', or 'py'. If omitted or null, searches by filename prefix across extensions.

returns.description: The full path of the first matching file, or 'No file found' if no match exists.

tools.name: open_file
tools.description: Opens a file at the specified Windows path using its default associated application. Returns the file path if opened, or 'No such file found' if the path does not exist or is not a file.

path.description: The full path to the file to open, such as 'C:\\Users\\User\\Documents\\report.pdf'.

returns.description: A success message containing the file path if opened, or 'No such file found' if the path does not exist or is not a file.

tools.name: open_an_app
tools.description: Launches a Windows executable (.exe) at the specified path. Returns the executable path if launched, or 'No such app found' if the path does not exist or does not point to an .exe file.

path.description: The full path to the executable to launch, such as 'C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe'.

returns.description: A success message containing the executable path if launched, or 'No such app found' if the path does not exist or is not an .exe file.

tools.name: run_a_generic_command
tools.description: Use this tool only for simple general purpose command execution. Do not use it otherwise if the command is too complex or if there are other more suitable tools.

cmd.description: The full Windows file related shell command to execute as a single string (supports shell features).

returns.description: Returns subprocess result object on success, error string on failure, or null if user denies execution.

tools.name: run_a_vbs_script
tools.description: Use this tool to perform simple Windows GUI automation, such as launching applications, activating or switching windows, simulating keyboard input with SendKeys, typing text, and interacting with basic menus or dialogs. Prefer this tool when a task requires human-like  interactions that cannot be achieved with a simple shell command.

script.description: The full VBScript source code to execute, as a single string. It is written to a temporary .vbs file and run with cscript. Use WScript.Echo to produce output.

returns.description: Returns subprocess result object (stdout, stderr, returncode) on success, error string on failure, or null if user denies execution.

tools.name: rename_file
tools.description: Renames an existing file on the filesystem. Requires the full path to the current file and a distinct new filename.

path.description: The FULL absolute path of the EXISTING file you want to rename (e.g., 'C:\Users\HP\Desktop\musketeer').

new_name.description: The brand NEW filename ONLY, without any directory path (e.g., 'ronin'). DO NOT pass a path here, and DO NOT reuse the old name.

tools.name: search_the_internet
tools.description: Searches the web for a query and returns the main extracted text content from the most relevant result as plain text.

query.description: The search query to look up online.

returns.description: Returns the extracted content from the best matching webpage as plain text, or an empty string if no useful content is found.
